# Restricted application identity observer —2026-10-29

An actual restricted PostgreSQL login can now use the candidate guarded Django transaction without broad metadata-role grants. The fixed observer exposes only cluster identifier and PGDATA; current/session role, database, endpoint and durability are read as the actual caller on the same connection. Existing operator behavior is retained, and production/bank-sandbox still select the connection-denying backend. This completes a local application-role prerequisite, not the full all-write/transport/deployment path.

[Final immutable source, logs and readback](../evidence/t02/application-observer-revisions/c3ef5f9232f6d0e179c205a622f6a0c5493b4757404069c616be1c8c5873bfa8.json) bind source b201c9a with dirty attribution, every changed producer/test/SQL/lock hash, all15 exact inert source files, actual commands/exits/timings and unchanged four-image output identities. Final real PostgreSQL18.6/Django/admission suite passes204 tests/3 checks/15.180s; source build/import/help/denial passes5 tests/7 checks/4.426s; deployment evaluation passes31 tests/16 checks/2.207s. Enclosing lane times are15.210s,4.466s and2.248s respectively. Twenty restricted-role cases are included in the204; they are not an additional test count.

## Behavior and authority boundary

`ops/postgresql/application-observer.sql` is inert source. It creates a new schema and zero-argument SQL SECURITY DEFINER function in one transaction, removes PUBLIC schema/function access before commit and supplies no login creation or grants. Existing objects are rejected, not adopted. Installation, function owner and the sole application-role grant require a separately approved bootstrap/policy path; none is installed by these files or the source package.

Before invoking the function, `application_observer.py` checks the exact schema/function/owner, raw body, signature/result types, language, stable/restricted/definer flags, secure search path and tightly limited schema/function ACLs. It rejects unknown/multiple functions, unexpected owner or schema ownership, PUBLIC/other-login/grant-option access and application role elevation, role membership, database ownership or public-schema CREATE. The owner name is an explicit trusted-policy input; binding it to approved immutable connection/application controls remains required. The existing identity/durability comparison is shared, not replaced with a caller assertion.

The actual server permits this ordinary login to call pg_control_system(); the protected field in the existing combined observer is data_directory. The first focused assertion incorrectly expected both direct operations to deny; it failed and was corrected to the observed privilege behavior. The new role has no superuser, CREATEDB, CREATEROLE, replication, bypass-RLS or role membership. Tests authenticate as that login through a private disposable Unix socket, not SET ROLE on a privileged connection. Local HBA uses isolated trust fixtures; this is not SCRAM/private production transport qualification.

`guarded_application_atomic` selects the fixed observer inside the existing durable Django transaction/admission lifetime. It requires an already connected registered wrapper, keeps the raw connection fixed, compares actual SQL/runtime identity before work and before commit, rejects deferred callbacks/rollback-only/reconnect/outer/manual transactions and retains the cooperative admission lease through actual commit/rollback. The original operator context still uses its original direct observer. No automatic backend interception, application/worker call-site switch, reconnect, retry, record issuance or host mount is added.

## Demonstrated security defect and correction

The first candidate's unqualified text cast and implicit temporary-schema ordering permitted a caller-created temporary text domain to run its check function with the definer owner's privileges. A real disposable PostgreSQL control inserted one synthetic owner-only canary row and failed the required zero-row assertion. The candidate was not deployed or committed before this correction.

All relevant types are now fully qualified as pg_catalog types, and the function explicitly places pg_temp last after pg_catalog. The same restricted caller's direct function call and the Python observer both return the actual identity with zero canary rows. That control passes in the final204-test suite. The final report retains the actual failed control and explicitly supersedes [the earlier19/203-test subset](../evidence/t02/application-observer-revisions/14648b28d4445ed6eaf79e23557805f3e96f1bd314e7072119b165f51c2ff3aa.json); earlier green subsets were insufficient security evidence. PostgreSQL's [SECURITY DEFINER guidance](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-createfunction.html#SQL-CREATEFUNCTION-SECURITY) requires careful trusted-schema ordering and removal of default PUBLIC execution. The fixed source follows those requirements; no generic security guarantee is inferred.

Controls also demonstrate two-statement/actual QuerySet create/update/delete commits, exception/runtime/durability/admission/late EXECUTE-revocation rollback, independent publisher exclusion through actual commit/rollback, changed body/search-path/invoker policy, invalid owner, missing function, PUBLIC/other-login/grant-option ACLs, unsafe schema grants, role elevation/membership, unrelated caller denial and existing-object refusal. The owner/admin must still cooperate with the admission lease: two client queries cannot stop a privileged noncooperating catalog change between policy validation and execution.

## Evidence and remaining scope

The inert source bundle `/nix/store/hw10skg9vb72a7v0ilsczsfd4v6y10yn-shop-database-tools-source` contains13 non-executable Python modules and two SQL files plus its manifest. Actual Nix build, exact byte/hash/closure comparison, isolated import, packaged help and mutation-denial checks pass. Its executable/runtime_qualified/production_activation fields remain false. All four runtime image paths are unchanged, retaining the [four-image/native SBOM proof](image-sbom-2026-10-29.md); this source bundle does not silently enter app/worker images. The earlier bundle is preserved as historical pre-security evidence.

Initial focused harness attempts accidentally selected full shared /tmp and stopped before any tests. The corrected harness sets dev_postgres.SCRATCH_PARENT to project-owned .scratch as the established checker does. An isolated original b201c9a Django-guard module then demonstrates missing new transaction integration without replacing any worktree source; final source is never rolled back. Raw results and the later temporary-domain failure are retained. Only owned disposable clusters/roles/tables and the existing owned Nix build scratch were used; no shared cleanup, .env, protected host/service or provider operation occurred.

The exact required checks are `nix develop --offline ./ops/nixos --command python3 scripts/check.py database-destination`, `database-tools` and `deployment-eval`, with the same project-owned TMPDIR/XDG cache and recorded owned build directory used by the [SBOM work](image-sbom-2026-10-29.md). Acceptance timeouts and durability settings are unchanged. Production backend bytes are unchanged; no full backend rebuild/lock suite is repeated.

No host /proc/control/management socket may enter app containers.
